items.title: Highlights from ESL Pro League S24 playoffs
items.summary: Follow the action as Counter-Strike returns to the Spodek.
items.text: MOUZ 's first pistol in the series, and what a time to get it. The captain takes things into his own hands to break Spirit 's economy and extend MOUZ 's lead to two. Four out of four pistols for Spirit in the series, and this one looks set to propel them to the Nuke decider. A good read by the Spirit CT side, but MOUZ picked their stack apart with some great shots. Despite winning and converting both pistols, Spirit couldn't trouble MOUZ on the opening map, with Ádám "⁠torzsi⁠" Torzsás crowning a fantastic performance with a post-plant 3k. An overly optimistic Danil "⁠donk⁠" Kryshkovets push gave Lotan "⁠Spinx⁠" Giladi and AK, and the Israeli rifler converted the gift to a 2k and a round for his team. Two Spirit rounds to end the half give the majority-Russian squad a chance, but MOUZ are still in the driver's seat. A 5vs3 secured after one of the weirdest Long fights of all time, and Spirit are forced into a save. In August, MOUZ lifted the BLAST Bounty S2 trophy after defeating Spirit in the grand final. That 3-1 victory ended both a seven-series losing against Spirit and a 17-month wait for a title. A month later, however, Spirit returned the favor by the same score in the Porto final, leaving MOUZ one step short of another trophy. At ESL Pro League Season 24, it was MOUZ 's turn to strike back. Their 2-0 group-stage victory secured a playoff berth and stopped Spirit 's 32 straight wins in Swiss groups. Now, just five days later, the two teams meet again at the Spodek for their 7th encounter of the year.

items.title: MOUZ beat Spirit en route to EPL final
items.summary: An unusually quiet series by donk paved the way for MOUZ's victory.
items.text: MOUZ became the second grand finalists of ESL Pro League Season 24 after defeating Spirit in a close-fought three-mapper (Dust2 13-7, Mirage 9-13, Nuke 13-11). The result marks MOUZ 's third grand final of the season, with Vitality standing between them and the trophy, while Spirit are set to meet Aurora in the third-place decider. "This win will give us a lot of confidence," Ádám "⁠torzsi⁠" Torzsás said in a post-match interview. "We are a new team, so I don't think it's going to be the same [as in 2025] against Vitality." The series began on Spirit 's pick of Dust2, where the Russian squad was found asleep at the wheel in the opening rounds. While they won and converted the pistol, Spirit found themselves 2-8 down before finally clicking into gear and won five in a row. MOUZ then won a crucial halfbuy after Danil "⁠donk⁠" Kryshkovets 's overpeek into Lower and took that momentum all the way to the bank, with torzsi crowning a fantastic performance with a post-plant 3k. Spirit showed a different face on Mirage, however, looking composed and, more importantly, buoyed by an online donk . The Russian phenom topped the board for his team with 19 kills on the map, while also putting the final nail in the MOUZ coffin with a 1vs2. Spirit kept up their flawless record in pistol rounds at the start of Nuke, but couldn't convert their success into a big lead. MOUZ , led by Oldřich "⁠PR⁠" Nový , quickly seized the lead and edged out a 7-5 half thanks to 17 frags by the Czech rifler. Spirit came back into the game after a pair of clutches by Andrey "⁠tN1R⁠" Tatarinovich and Myroslav "⁠zont1x⁠" Plakhotia , but PR 's unrelenting fragging continued. items.title: FaZe defeat NAVI Junior twice to secure Roman Imperium Cup IX championship
items.summary: FaZe had to overcome a 1-0 deficit in the upper bracket final.
items.text: FaZe have won Roman Imperium Cup IX after beating NAVI Junior in two seperate matchups on the tournament's final day. The first one came in the upper final, where FaZe reverse swept NAVI Junior to secure a spot in the grand final. NAVI Junior showed resolve, bouncing back in the consolidation final v. Sangal to set up a rematch v. FaZe. Their second matchup was completely different, as FaZe dominated from start to finish to defeat the NAVI academy squad 2-0 in the grand final. NAVI Junior elected to start the upper final on Anubis. NAVI Junior held a slight 7-5 lead on the CT side after a back-and-forth first half. Four rounds in a row put NAVI Junior up 11-5 early in the second half, and the lead would be too much for FaZe to overcome. NAVI held on to win the first map 13-9 and take a 1-0 lead. The second map was FaZe's Nuke pick, where they would jump out to a 7-2 advantage on the less-favored T side. NAVI Junior battled back to even things up at 7-7 early in their own T side. From there, FaZe ground out the win to take the map 13-9 and even the series 1-1. The decider was Dust2, where NAVI Junior sprinted to an 8-4 halftime lead. After going up 11-6, NAVI Junior's campaign ground to a halt. FaZe mounted the comeback to force overtime, eventually taking the map 19-15 and the series 2-1 behind David "frozen" Čerňanský's 31 map-three frags. The second series featured the same mapset, but a very different story. NAVI Junior's Anubis pick went entirely the way of FaZe, as Russell "Twistzz" Van Dulken's troops ran away with a 10-2 T side, winning the map 13-2.

items.title: FaZe knocking on the door of top 15 with Roman Imperium Cup IX title
items.summary: Twistzz's charges have one foot in the Singapore Major after an unbeaten run in Vila Nova de Gaia.
items.text: FaZe won the Roman Imperium Cup IX on Saturday after a 2-0 thrashing of NAVI Junior , moving up 14 places in the global VRS to 16th. Russel "⁠Twistzz⁠" Van Dulken 's charges now have a 71.8% chance of qualifying for PGL Major Singapore, according to HLTV's latest projections . They will attend two more LAN events before the November 2 invite cutoff: DraculaN Season 7 (October 19-23) in Bucharest, and RLG Tesla Cup (October 27-29) in Belgrade. It was FaZe ’s first LAN title since IEM Chengdu 2024, with David "⁠frozen⁠" Čerňanský the sole member left from that squad. Their previous LAN final, at HLC Belgrade PRO 2026, ended in a loss to BIG that cost them a place at the IEM Cologne Major. FaZe capped their Roman Imperium Cup IX run with a one-sided series in which they conceded only four rounds. The campaign was far from straightforward, though, as they had to recover from a map down against Sangal in the opening round and again against NAVI Junior in the upper bracket final, where the decider went to overtime.

items.title: ECL S52 NA Cup 3 Day 3 recap: Villainous and Desi Boyz eliminated early
items.summary: Four more teams have been knocked out of the event.
items.text: Cup 3 of ESL Challenger League Season 52 continued with four matches going down yesterday, all in the lower bracket. Only eight teams remain in the $17,500 online event. Club 333 and Villainous lost their series 0-2 to DETONATE and regain, respectively. After making the top four of Cup 2, FarmVille were knocked out early after a 1-2 loss to Wanted Goons. Likewise, Desi Boyz, with Justin "jsfeltner" Feltner subbing for Saad "Pluto" Siraj, lost 1-2 to EMPIRE. The series began on Villainous's pick of Anubis, with regain losing the pistol and conversion. regain rebounded with a seven-round streak before a final three from Villainous closed the gap to 7-5. regain won the second pistol and conversion before Villainous got four to tie the score 9-9. regain went on a 4-1 run down the stretch to take their opponent's pick 13-10. regain picked Inferno and won the first pistol and conversion. The two teams then traded streaks before a final win from Villainous tied the score 6-6. After winning their CT pistol, regain had a nearly flawless second half en route to a 13-7 victory, eliminating Villainous. EMPIRE picked Dust2 as the first map, but struggled in the early game as they went down 3-6 despite winning the pistol. They closed the gap a bit, but still trailed slightly at 5-7 going into the next half. The second half started back and forth to bring the score to 8-10 before EMPIRE took control, getting five in a row to secure Dust2 13-10. Desi Boyz picked Mirage, but EMPIRE got the pistol and put them down 1-3 early. Desi Boyz found a four-round streak, but the first half ended with the teams tied 6-6. items.title: Sashi register for NSTLGA Texas Open
items.summary: The EU-turned-AU team is coming to... NA?
items.text: Following their controversial transition to the Asia region, Sashi have unexpectedly registered for NTSLGA's San Antonio event, which begins October 30th. Earlier this month, Sashi attempted to replicate BC.Game's swap to the less competitive Asia region by signing two Australian players to short-term contracts, in addition to taking advantage of Anton "⁠Anlelele⁠" Huynh's Vietnamese citizenship. On October 6th, Valve responded to Sashi's bold move to qualify to PGL Major Singapore with new rules , which would bar the team from qualifying at all. While BC.Game were granted an exception to the new edicts, Sashi's Major eligibility is still in question. Since Valve's crackdown, the Danish organization has signed New Zealand's Michael "⁠chelleos⁠" Hawkins, seeing the team fully commit to an Asian core. It's worth noting that Sashi are also registered for (but unlikely to attend) HyperX Retake Season 13 in Portugal, which begins just one day before the NSTLGA Texas Open. items.title: Vitality beat Aurora to reach EPL final
items.summary: apEX's troops will go up against Spirit or MOUZ in Sunday's title decider.
items.text: Vitality are through to the grand final of ESL Pro League 24 following a come-from-behind victory against Aurora , who burned bright on the opening map of Anubis thanks to a great performance from Özgür "⁠woxic⁠" Eker but couldn't play with the same intensity in the rest of the series. Vitality 's victory was anchored by a standout performance from star player Mathieu "⁠ZywOo⁠" Herbaut , who bounced back from a quiet first map to post a series-high 1.44 rating, driven largely by a 2.36 rating on Cache, his highest ever on the map. Vitality will contest the final against the winner of Spirit vs. MOUZ . It will be the chance for the three-time Major champions to win their second trophy of the season before Dan "⁠apEX⁠" Madesclaire temporarily steps down from the roster for PGL Masters Bucharest. Neither team could pull away in the first half of Anubis, trading three-round streaks. Vitality twice appeared on course for a sizeable lead, only for Ismailcan "⁠XANTARES⁠" Dörtkardeş and woxic to halt the momentum with big individual plays. Heading into the second half, Ashley "⁠ash⁠" Battye hailed his players' reaction to Vitality 's early aggression. "We played really, really, really well. I'm very happy with how we played. Very, very impressed," the British coach said, asking them to keep it up in the second half. Aurora 's players followed the coach's instructions and took control of the game from the initial exchanges. A lapse in communication cost them an important round against a shoddy buy, but they remained composed and put the game to rest, with woxic posting a jaw-dropping 3.13 CT rating.

items.title: Marsborne, regain, and LAG among notable signups as NSTLGA Emerald Cup registration closes
items.summary: The scaling prize pool got up to $2,500.
items.text: On October 9th, the two-day registration window for the NSTLGA Emerald Cup closed with a solid 37 of the potential 64 spots being filled. The team list is a strong one, with many noteworthy squads in the region like Marsborne, regain, and LAG securing a spot. The event will begin in just under a week on October 16th and run through October 18th. The prize pool scaled with the number of teams, so only half of the potential $5,000 pot will be available. The online event will be run through FACEIT, with every team starting from a double-elimination group stage. Advancing teams will then go to a single-elimination playoff bracket to determine the winner. All matches in the event will be best-of-three. The event will also be the second event after NSTLGA Season 2, contributing to the tournament organizer's new circuit. $5,000 is on the line as teams earn points through the rest of NSTLGA's events in 2026. The Emerald Cup is one of two events with the smallest 1x points multiplier, but it is still an opportunity for teams to climb the leaderboard. items.title: BBL confirm MistR signing
items.summary: The 22-year-old will debut for the Turkish organization on Tuesday.
items.text: BBL have announced that they have completed the signing of former Sashi member Mikkel "⁠MistR⁠" Thomsen , replacing Jonas "⁠Boye⁠" Boye Østergaard , who has been moved to the bench. MistR 's future had been up in the air since he and Casper "⁠Cabbi⁠" Jensen were benched by Sashi in favor of Australian duo Tynan "⁠TjP⁠" Purtell and Jordan "⁠Hatz⁠" Bajic as the organization opted to switch to the Asian VRS region. The 22-year-old then announced that he had mutually parted ways with Sashi , thanking the organization for allowing him "to step away from this crazy situation." His signing marks the first change to BBL 's roster since the Turkish organization entered Counter-Strike with the acquisition of the BBL roster. "His impact was noticeable from the very first practice sessions, bringing a new level of energy and intensity to the team," team manager Derya Üçpınar told HLTV. "We believe that overcoming the challenges he has faced will only make him stronger, and we’re excited to support him as he takes this next step with BBL. "We’re building this project with long-term ambitions, and we’re confident that MistR will be an important part of what we aim to achieve." BBL are currently ranked 38th in the global VRS following a semi-final run at ROG JOURNEY Autumn, where they notably beat BC.Game in the playoffs. Stake Pulse Beat III and DraculaN Season 7 will offer them two more chances to pick up Valve points before the November 2 invite cut-off for the Singapore Major. items.title: Short news: Week 40
items.summary: Catch up with more Counter-Strike news in bite-sized pieces.
items.text: Rasmus "⁠kreaz⁠" Johansson has announced that he is no longer part of INFINITE , leaving the team down to three players following last month's departure of Martin "⁠Dytor⁠" Handl . The team is expected to announce their replacements soon, with their NODWIN Clutch Series 13 and Digital Crusade DraculaN S7 campaigns taking place over the course of October. Raul "⁠Blytz⁠" Gligor Sebastian "⁠volt⁠" Maloș Henrich "⁠sl3nd⁠" Hevesi Nordic Partners have announced that they have mutually agreed to part ways with Ville "⁠myltsi⁠" Vilkman , citing "overlapping roles and similar strengths within the roster." The Finnish player, formerly of ENCE , is the second player to leave NPG this week, following the departure of Mikkel "⁠Maze⁠" Sparvath on Wednesday. Nils "⁠k1to⁠" Gruhne Max "⁠Marix⁠" Kugener Maciej "⁠Muciek⁠" Mordal Jonathan "⁠MusambaN1⁠" Torrent (coach) David "⁠Kairi⁠" de Miguel (assistant coach) Valve has released an update overnight, with a decrease to the AUG reload time the standout change. Added a ping icon for dropped defuse kits Reduced the time for AUG reload by half second Fixed the sound event during silent reload for Desert Eagle Fixed a case of buzzing soundscape sounds during demo playback Daniel "⁠sprayxd⁠" Kogan has taken over as head coach of BIG Academy as Timo "⁠Spiidi⁠" Richter "has decided to focus on his academic path." sprayxd 's last head coaching endeavour saw him at the helm of Young Ninjas , before he became an assistant coach for the main team. SemperFi has announced the signing of former illwill rifler Cristian "⁠7Kick⁠" Dragos Radut , who joins the sole remaining member from the organization's previous roster, James "⁠SaVage⁠" Savage , amidst a rebuild.
